title: Individual glycemic responses to carbohydrates vary and reflect underlying metabolic physiology (Olink)
projectDescription: Proteomics data was measured by using the Olink Explore 1536 panel from baseline plasma sample. The project is also supported by Themistocles L Assimes (Stanford University tassimes@stanford.edu) and Fahim Abbasi (Stanford University, fahim@stanford.edu).
sampleProcessingProtocol: Blood samples were collected at the Clinical and Translational Research Unit (CTRU). Participants were recruited from the San Francisco Bay Area, California with a balanced sex (based on self-report) ratio. Inclusion criteria were that participants were over 18 years old and not pregnant. Exclusion criteria include major organ diseases, hypertension (bp>160/100mmHg), pregnant or lactating, use of diabetogenic medications, malabsorptive disorders (e.g., celiac sprue), heavy alcohol use, use of weight loss medications or specific diets, weight change of more than 2 kg in the last three weeks, and a history of bariatric surgery. Additionally, individuals were excluded if they had any medical condition that physicians believed would interfere with study participation or evaluation of results. Individuals with mental incapacity and/or cognitive impairment that would preclude adequate understanding of or cooperation with the study protocol were also excluded. Details are available in clinicaltrials.gov (NCT03919877). The study protocol was reviewed and approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) at Stanford University School of Medicine Human Research Protection Office (Institutional Review Board # 43883). All participants provided written informed consent. Blood samples were collected in EDTA tubes after an overnight fast. Immediately after collection, the samples were centrifuged at 4°C for 15 minutes at 3000 RPM. The plasma was extracted from the centrifuged samples and divided into aliquots that were stored at -80°C. The samples were kept frozen until the proteomic analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: Proteomics data was measured by using the Olink Explore 1536 panel from plasma sample and normalized as Normalized Protein eXpression (NPX). Proximity extension antibody assays were used to quantify protein expression levels. Quality control was performed by identifying outliers within each protein panel by principal component analysis and by assessment of median and interquartile range values for normalized NPX across protein samples. This analysis was performed using the OlinkAnalyze package in R, which was developed and maintained by the Olink Proteomics Data Science Team.
